rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance
rules_evaluated.evidence: No instances of banned words (honest, delve, landscape-verb, importantly, crucial, substrate, leverage-verb, synergize, paradigm shift) detected in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: No instances of ritual, practice(noun), or ceremony in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography
rules_evaluated.evidence: No date markers (2026-), stale-state callouts, or biography transitions present in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 lecture body uses appropriate quintet register: factual/direct (Boris tone on permission mechanics), logical/strategic (Martin on plan-review leverage), peer-warm (Godin in equals-not-pupils framing), insightful (Rory reframe on structure/appearance). No consultancy register.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 35 credits Dex Horthy for non-goals criterion parenthetically. Other four criteria presented as house synthesis (pedagogically sound—backing block documents which criteria are practitioner-sourced vs synthesized).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body
rules_evaluated.evidence: Consistent second person throughout (line 13: 'You press', line 46-47: 'Your read'). No delivery mechanics or teacher-POV narration. No 'the student' or 'the trainer' in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms introduced with earned context: 'soft item' (line 47: 'the step that reads clean but skips over something'); 'walk-down' (line 47: 'the agent's walk-down catch different misses'). No maintainer-only vocabulary leaking into body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance shapes detected (no 'no penalty', 'fine way to', 'it's OK if'). Authority voice maintained throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single practitioner mention: Dex Horthy at line 35 for non-goals criterion. Complies with one-mention-per-module ceiling for this lecture.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream
rules_evaluated.evidence: Punchy framings maintained without softening: 'Five things a good plan has' (line 29), 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' (line 39), 'Two reads, paired' (line 45). No hedging or carve-out needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body
rules_evaluated.evidence: No positioning-defend phrases ('not an aspirational X', 'not a vendor Y', 'grounded in actual'). Pedagogical observations only (structure-appearance distinction, specificity matters).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early
rules_evaluated.evidence: M2 lecture introducing plan-mode reading skills. Terminology earned at point of use: 'permission state' (line 13, explained operationally), 'read-only' (line 13, defined with capability list), 'Shift+Tab' (line 13, named key), 'status bar' (line 13, identified target). No premature jargon from M3+.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function
rules_evaluated.evidence: Section closers checked for dangling pronouns and bypass-the-agent commands: line 37 'Five things. That's the read.' (punchy, no danglers); line 51 forward-looking statement with 'you' as subject. No dangling pronouns or forced student actions outside prompts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose
rules_evaluated.evidence: Agent interactions use peer verbs: line 22 'ask Claude to describe' (gentle, collaborative). No combative verbs (bark, command, force, drag, push).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism
rules_evaluated.evidence: All headers literal and mechanism-true: 'Plan mode is a read-only permission state' (line 11—TRUE), 'Optional: ask plan mode directly' (line 18—TRUE), 'Five things a good plan has' (line 29—TRUE), 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' (line 39—TRUE), 'Two reads, paired' (line 45—TRUE), 'Find is easier than judge' (line 53—TRUE), 'Plan review is a high-leverage gate' (line 58—TRUE).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — empty negation, deictic drumroll, bold-label echo, citation duplication
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negations (negations work against reader's actual priors). No deictic drumroll. No bold-label echo. No citation duplication. Example: line 31 'Not "update the config."' negates against likely vague approach, not empty.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap framing ('you're missing', 'you already think'). Body teaches reading discipline without assuming prior shortcoming.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use
rules_evaluated.evidence: All core terms earned with operational definitions: 'plan mode' (line 11—defined as permission state + mechanism), 'permission state' (line 13—explained operationally), 'read-only' (line 13—specified capabilities), 'Shift+Tab' (line 13—named key), 'status bar' (line 13—what to watch). Terms sufficiently grounded for M2 placement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — recovery / troubleshooting branches not in lecture
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture body contains no troubleshooting, recovery paths, or 'what-if' branches. Teaching-only narrative.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 27 'Watch what comes back' is observational (emotional payoff, tool literacy), not error-catching. No manual verification tasks in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent
rules_evaluated.evidence: All student actions remain in agent conversation: line 20 'Enter plan mode in your own session right now', line 22 'Ask Claude to describe what changed'. No editor/terminal/file-editing primitives.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences
rules_evaluated.evidence: No em-dashes detected in body. Sentences are short and direct. Complex ideas split into separate simple sentences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 18 'Optional: ask plan mode directly'—contains command verb 'ask'. Note: lecture sections are exempt from verb-header requirement (canonical architecture allows declarative noun-phrase headers for teaching-comprehension sections per §17 carve-out).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow
rules_evaluated.evidence: No contemplative-pause frames ('Pause before', 'Meta-moment', 'Step back', 'breathe', 'let it land'). Reflection is embedded in action, not announced.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward
rules_evaluated.evidence: All content serves teaching: criteria teach judgment, pressures teach discrimination, two-reads section teaches collaboration discipline. No administrative asides or implementation details before point of use.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 51: 'After you've done it once, you'll feel when a plan needs the second read'—'you' as grammatical subject, future-tense prospect. No audience-shift or generic 'they'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 22 provides action lead-in: 'Ask Claude to describe what changed in its behaviour when plan mode turned on.' Semantic, <20 words, precedes {{prompt:when-a-plan-is-good-1}} marker.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt is referenced by registry marker {{prompt:when-a-plan-is-good-1}} at line 24. Inline fenced prompts are not present (all references are markers). Correct registry-reference pattern.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer block (line 86-87) states mood target: 'anticipation toward grounded competence.' Body honors this: concrete criteria teach grounding, three-pressures section teaches discrimination (sharpening competence), tone is matter-of-fact and moving forward. Mood lived, not advertised (per rule 11, appropriate).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode
rules_evaluated.evidence: Positive-discipline section comes first ('Five things a good plan has'—line 29). Negative-pressure section (line 39) follows and serves as counter-balance to teach discrimination, not primary framing. Design is pedagogically sound: teach positive first, then show what fools you.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check
rules_evaluated.evidence: M2 lecture on plan-mode reading. No front-running of downstream modules (M3+ concepts not named). Content aligns with M2 scope (reading skills, approval discipline) per maintainer block line 86 pedagogy note.
